affectedPublicSurfaces: The AGENT TOOL REGISTRY for `optimize_product_2` gains TWO READ/AUTO specs in the product domain (#1704's domain registry): `get_product_diagnosis` over Product Information Issue Diagnosis (`GET /product/202405/products/diagnoses`) and `check_listing_rewrite` over Diagnose-and-Optimize (`POST /product/202411/products/diagnose_optimize`, used as a PRE-SUBMIT check on a rewrite the agent is about to propose). READ/AUTO is load-bearing: neither tool may carry `ToolPolicy.CONFIRM`, because a run that pauses to read is a run whose consent model has changed.

The PLAYBOOK `services/agent/playbooks/optimize_product.py` gains steps 0a and 0b AHEAD of the existing SEO step, so the order becomes diagnosis read → SEO words → suggestions → one lever (ADR-090 d.3). Today's committed order is step 1 listing read (`get_product_information`), step 2+3 SEO (`get_seo_keywords`), step 4/4.5 image inspect, step 5 listing write, step 6.5 status check — the existing step ids and intents must survive the insertion unchanged; only the ordering and the two new steps move.

The RUN'S TOOL LEDGER, which is what a seller and an operator actually observe: two new READ rows appear per run, and the FIRST tool call recorded becomes the diagnosis read. `services/agent/runner/ledger.py` writes `ToolExecution.tool_name` as the registered name, so the two names become countable in the ledger the moment they register. No route contract changes and no response model moves.

The RUN STATE: diagnosis codes and the codes a candidate rewrite clears are carried on `workflow_runs.state` for later steps and for the proposal. This is a JSON blob write on an existing column — no new column, no new table.

The ADR-070 INBOUND CHOKEPOINT gains a SANITISER ADAPTER for this surface. Diagnosis codes and suggestion text arrive as `vendor`-source free text: capped, truncation-signalled, and passed to the model as DATA in a tool-result role, never as an instruction role. This is the prompt-injection surface of the whole slice — a vendor string that reaches the model as an instruction is the failure this adapter exists to prevent.

The DEGRADED PATH is a seller-visible surface. When the shop does not hold `seller.product.optimize`, `ProductsResource` refuses BEFORE transport with `ScopeMissing` (from #1714's persisted scopes and `has_scope`) — no HTTP call is attempted at all — the run does NOT fail, and the seller-facing text carries the `scope_unavailable` wording through the ADR-070 outbound banned-pattern guard. `scope_unavailable` is a STOP-REASON NAME, not the seller's words: the Vietnamese copy says the diagnosis could not be read and that Juli used its own scoring, and it must never leak the identifier itself (S-NFR-4).

NO HTTP surface changes: nothing under `backend/src/juli_backend/api/routes/` is opened, no `/v1/**` or `/demo/**` request or response model moves. Nothing under `apps/`, `packages/` or `ios/` is touched — this epic's doNotLoad list.

CONSUMED, NOT BUILT: the two resource methods, their guard allowlist entries and their sandbox captures belong to #1716 (integrations); the persisted OAuth scopes, `has_scope` and `ScopeMissing` belong to #1714. If this slice finds itself editing `integrations/tiktok/capabilities.py`, `constants.py` or `resources/products.py`, the routing was wrong — stop and report rather than re-adding them.

Mixed-version hazard: `juli-api` and `juli-celery-worker` must move onto the same release together. A stable worker without the two READ specs cannot execute a run whose playbook demands them, so the retained-stable rollback below assumes both processes move as one.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE. No column, index, constraint, table or grant is touched and NO Alembic revision file is created — the executor must not open `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`. The diagnosis codes and the cleared-code list live on the EXISTING `workflow_runs.state` JSON blob, and the two new tool names are values in the existing `tool_executions.tool_name` column, never enum members or CHECK-constraint entries. Stable and candidate therefore run the identical schema and coexist on one database: a stable process reading a run whose state carries the new keys simply ignores them, and a candidate reading a stable-written run finds them absent and takes the no-codes path.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing about the deployed system changes: the workflow keeps its SEO-first step order, no diagnosis is read, no scope is consulted, and the two tools do not exist to be called. That is today's state — nothing exposed, nothing partially applied, no vendor call made, no data hazard.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Code-only rollback: redeploy the previous release and restart `juli-api` AND `juli-celery-worker` together. There is no schema to revert and no downgrade to run — this slice owns no migration. The two tools disappear from the registry and the playbook returns to the SEO-first order. Runs COMPLETED under the candidate stay valid and readable: their `tool_executions` rows keep the two diagnosis names (unknown to the reverted registry but harmless — they are strings in a ledger, never a foreign key), and their `workflow_runs.state` keeps the code keys, which the reverted code simply does not read. A run SUSPENDED at CONFIRM across the rollback resumes correctly because consent is bound by `params_sha` over the tool call's arguments and neither the arguments nor the hash function move here — assert this pre-merge rather than assuming it. No vendor state was written at any point, so there is no vendor-side effect a revert fails to undo.

acceptanceCommands: ruff check backend tests scripts && ruff format --check backend tests scripts
doNotInfer: Do NOT add, restore or call a BASE-PRICE WRITE. `update_product_price` left this workflow in #1773 and `resources.products.update_prices` must have no caller on this path — not as a fallback, not behind CONFIRM, not in a fixture. This slice adds no write tool at all.
Do NOT let the MODEL choose a depth, a price or any number. This slice registers two READ tools; there is no numeric parameter for a model to pick, and reaching for one means drifting into #1778.

Do NOT introduce a DEFAULT SHOP MAXIMUM or any default discount depth as a placeholder. The shop maximum is #1775's required seller-confirmed setting; a default shipped untouched is a number no seller ever saw.

Do NOT claim a TIKTOK TIER OR CODE the API did not return (OP-NFR-2). The Price Diagnostics tier and the 14 card-diagnostic recommendations are NEVER claimed — no API exposes them, and listing-quality tier is US-only. 'TikTok flags…' may appear only where a code was actually returned; the degraded path must say Juli used its own scoring, never borrow TikTok's authority (ADR-090 d.3).

Do NOT reach for SEARCH ACTIVITIES. `POST /promotion/202309/activities/search` does not exist as a usable read (contract-collection A-25; `endpoints.md:509`), nothing here needs it, and no test may stub it into existence.

Do NOT enable or lean on REPEAT CONSENT. Optimize Product is barred from it in v1 (ADR-090 d.6, narrowing ADR-055 d.19). Two AUTO reads must not be described or tested as reducing the need for a fresh approval.

Do NOT read a MIGRATION NUMBER from head — do not write a migration at all. This slice has no schema change. Never run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive a number from the newest filename. Migration numbers are RESERVED BY META.

Do NOT re-add #1716's or #1714's work. The path constants, the `capabilities.py` allowlist entries, the `ProductsResource` methods and the captures are #1716's; the persisted OAuth scopes, `has_scope` and `ScopeMissing` are #1714's. Consume them. A diff that widens the guard allowlist here has crossed a domain boundary — stop and report.

Do NOT let a MISSING SCOPE and a VENDOR ERROR share a path. `ScopeMissing` degrades; a vendor error surviving retry is a real failure on the existing terminal. Mapping the second onto the first would hide a broken integration behind an honest-looking degrade.
Do NOT attempt the diagnosis HTTP call when the scope is absent. The refusal happens BEFORE transport; a 403 round trip is not the same guarantee and leaks a call the seller did not authorise.

Do NOT pass VENDOR TEXT to the model as an instruction. Codes and suggestion text are `vendor`-source DATA through the ADR-070 inbound chokepoint — capped, truncation-signalled, tool-result role. Never interpolated into a system prompt, a playbook intent or copy.

Do NOT put an internal identifier in seller-facing text. `scope_unavailable` is a stop-reason name; the seller reads Vietnamese, second person, through the outbound banned-pattern guard, with no projected impact magnitude and no causal claim (S-NFR-4).
Do NOT hand-edit the golden or the prompt snapshot to make a gate green. Regenerate once with the real runner and review the diff.
Do NOT touch `apps/**`, `ios/**`, `packages/**`, `docs/product/design/**` or the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051) — this epic's doNotLoad list.

Bind every test collaborator to the REAL object's signature — the real `ProductsResource` methods from #1716, the real `ToolRegistry`, the real `WorkflowRunner`, the existing fake LLM adapter over `LLMService.complete`. A `**kwargs` double proves routing, never that the real call would work.
